title: The digital detox paradox: Why Gen Z still wants brands in real life
summary: Unpacking Gen Z marketing trends at Advertising Week New York 2026: How digital fatigue, nostalgia and tactile experiences shape brand connection.
body_markdown:
Advertising Week New York is never short on provocative programming. At this year’s event, which took place Oct. 5–8, the industry’s most pressing topics were front-and-center on the Insights Stage — a space reserved for deep dives into trending ideas with “takeaways that \[marketers\] can immediately implement,” per the conference organizers.


Among the highlights: “The Digital Detox Paradox,” a panel discussion about recent shifts in behavior (and spending habits) among Gen Z and millennials. While younger consumers continue to discover, engage and shop online,


[new research from The Harris Poll, presented by Quad](https://www.quad.com/insights/consumer-insights/4-takeaways-for-marketers-on-the-human-advantage) ,


also reveals they’re increasingly screen-fatigued and tech-weary — and


[seeking out brands that prioritize the physical realm](https://www.quad.com/engage/the-return-of-touch) .


Moderated by Quad’s Max Prince, the panel featured some of the sharpest minds at the intersection of branding, strategy, data science and experiential marketing: Libby Rodney, Chief Strategy Officer at


[The Harris Poll](https://theharrispoll.com/) , a leading market research and analytics firms; Michelle Wong, Senior VP of Global Marketing for the toy company


[Jazwares](https://www.jazwares.com/) ; and Karen Robinovitz, Co-founder of the


[Sloomoo Institute](https://www.sloomoo.com/) , the viral slime brand known for its immersive pop-ups.


Here are three key takeaways for the marketers who weren’t in attendance.

## 2. The physical vs. digital binary is dead


Marketers see these divisions, but the so-called digital natives are, in truth, omnichannel consumers. The Sloomoo Institute’s Robinovitz pointed to a recent event series that invited customers to meet influencers in brick-and-mortar spaces: “All of the kids who came were so excited to be with these creators in real life in order to make content with them.” And Jazwares’ Wong cited one of her company’s most popular products: a wristband that dispenses stickers. While YouTube provided a critical platform for discovery, the IRL community that supports collecting and trading those stickers has become the tangible growth catalyst for Jazwares.


Both Robinovitz and Wong argued for better channel integration, not channel agnosticism. And market research from The Harris Poll supports that strategic mindset:


[84% of Gen Z and millennials value brands that seamlessly blend technology with physical experiences](https://www.quad.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/the-harris-poll-quad-the-return-of-touch-report-2025.pdf) .
